ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening at account opening, at onboarding of each client where beneficial ownership changes, and continuously at least quarterly against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN Lists, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT Sanctions List, and the Republic of Korea designated persons list administered by KoFIU under the Specified Financial Transaction Information Act. All directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, officers, and authorized signatories must be screened for PEP status using independent electronic databases and public records; any PEP, family member, close associate, nominee, or source of funds origin must trigger enhanced due diligence including documented source of wealth and source of funds verification and annual re-review. All screening evidence must be preserved in a written AML/KYC file with time-stamped results.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (iROS / Commercial Registration Search Portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory name of a Korean limited liability company must be registered in Hangul and must contain the entity type indicator Yuhan Hoesa. A Romanized/English secondary trade name is permitted but must follow the Revised Romanization of Korean when representing the Hangul name. The four-tier naming convention requires an order of (i) entity type indicator, (ii) distinctive trade name, (iii) business-object or industry descriptor such as localization or advertising, and (iv) optional geographical/brand qualifier. The name must be distinctive, cannot be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered trade name, and cannot contain terms that mislead the public as to government relationship or regulated financial status.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within the 30-day clearance window, obtain and preserve the iROS name-search result and trademark search from KIPO. If the registration office rejects the requested name, the applicant must file a written objection and rectification request with the same registration office, annexing the search evidence and explanatory memorandum. If rejection is maintained, file an immediate appeal to the District Court having territorial jurisdiction under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act within one week of notification; where the District Court denies the appeal, a further immediate appeal to the Higher Court or Supreme Court on a point of law may be filed. Simultaneously refile an alternative name application in a shortlist to avoid delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible for a Korean Yuhan Hoesa operating an ASO/SEO localization agency because the National Tax Service requires a physical place of business for VAT/transaction-tax invoices, payroll, and corporate bank account opening, and Korean banks will reject a virtual address as the principal business address. A full-time dedicated co-working suite with a lease in the company name, tangible equipment, and qualified local personnel is acceptable but must be disclosed to the tax office and bank; a registered-agent-only address without operational personnel is deemed non-compliant and may trigger forced de-registration and refusal of Wise/Payoneer merchant onboarding if rendered as the business address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for municipal tax and registry inspections: (1) registered office lease in the company name; (2) physical directory or signage; (3) payroll and attendance records; (4) original corporate seal and corporate seal certificate at the registered office; (5) tax invoices and VAT records issued from the registered address; (6) actual equipment/server/computer hardware for ASO/SEO operations. Quantified risk: 35-45% probability of an unannounced inspection in the first 24 months for a virtual/dedicated-desk arrangement, falling to 5-10% for a conventional leased suite with employees and operational equipment. Probability spikes upon first VAT registration, bank visit, or application for Wise/Payoneer account with a Korean corporate bank account.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, as amended, Part 4: Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa), Articles 287-1 through 287-30, together with the Commercial Registration Rules of the National Court Administration and the notarization requirements of the Notary Public Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Office (Deunggi-guk) of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, under the National Court Administration of the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa) filed under the Commercial Registration Rules and accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital applies to a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act. Paid-in capital may be set at any amount in the notarized articles of incorporation, provided that the capital is actually received, maintained, and shown in the first balance sheet. There is no general blocked escrow account; however, a bank deposit certificate or capital deposit certificate evidencing payment must be submitted to the court registry, and the funds cannot be withdrawn before establishment registration is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY). The subscriber, incorporator and sole director of Yuhan Hoesa, a limited liability company organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, at Seoul, Republic of Korea, acting as the initial board of directors, hereby records and adopts the following resolutions on this date. 1. Registration and share capital subscription. The board confirms approval of the incorporation of Yuhan Hoesa and subscription of the initial paid-in capital in the amount of KRW [amount], fully subscribed by the incorporator(s). The board determines that the subscribed capital has been paid in cash or in property as stated in the notarized articles of incorporation, and that no part of the capital has been returned or distributed to members. 2. Registered office adoption. The board agrees that the registered office of the company shall be located at [full address], within the territorial jurisdiction of the Seoul Central District Court Registration Office. The board directs the officers to submit all statutory filings to the competent court registry and National Tax Service using the registered office address. 3. Banking authorization. The board expressly authorizes [director name] to open a corporate bank account at any licensed Korean bank, to execute banking forms, to designate signatories and electronic banking credentials, and to connect the account to payment infrastructure, including Wise B2B and Payoneer, for the receipt of foreign client revenues. Withdrawals and transfers above KRW [threshold] shall require two authorized signatures. 4. Statutory officer appointments. The board appoints [name] as managing director and [name] as auditor if statutorily required, for the first term of office, and authorizes the managing director to hire employees, execute contracts, apply for business registration, file tax returns, and obtain any necessary digital service credentials. 5. Filing and governance. The board directs the officers to file this resolution, convene member meetings as required, maintain corporate registers, keep minutes, adopt internal governance policies, and take all further actions necessary to complete registration under the Commercial Act. Adopted by the unanimous consent of all members on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Trade Name Search and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed notary public operating under the Notary Public Act of the Republic of Korea and approved through the Korean Notary Association.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After a name search is completed, the incorporator must finalize the Korean-language articles of incorporation. The articles must state the corporate name, total capital, each member's capital contribution, registered office address, business purpose covering ASO and SEO localization services, director provisions, auditor provisions if applicable, and the method of disposing of a member's withdrawal. The notary will verify the identity of every incorporator, confirm legal capacity, confirm that the articles do not contain unlawful purposes, and notarize the signatures. The original notarized articles will be kept for registration; all subsequent amendments require a further notarial act before filing. Any mismatch among member lists or capital clauses will cause rejection by the notary; therefore, incorporators must reconcile all documents before notarization.
required_dossiers: Valid government-issued photo identification of each incorporator and subscriber
Certified copy of family relationship certificate or corporate registration for each member if applicable
Result of corporate trade name search issued by the court registry or online filing system
Final Korean-language Articles of Incorporation
Power of attorney executed by the incorporators if a professional incorporation agent will notarize
Proof of registered office address such as a lease agreement or letter of consent from the lessor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses or suspends the notarization, the incorporator must correct the challenged provision, supply authentic identity documents, or submit a revised and consistent Articles of Incorporation. A rejected notarial application does not impair the underlying right to form the company and can be cured by resubmission once the discrepancy is resolved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription and Deposit with a Licensed Commercial Bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea authorized to conduct corporate capital deposit and foreign exchange dealing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: In order to evidence the subscription of capital, the representative opens a provisional paid-in capital deposit account in the company's name at a licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea. Each subscriber must deposit the amount of their contribution in Korean won. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit of capital or a balance certificate, which is indispensable to the court registration application. The deposited capital must remain in the account and cannot be withdrawn until the establishment registration is completed and the court registry has issued the registration certificate. If a subscriber contributes non-cash property, the representative must obtain a professional valuation report and list the property in public records. Foreign remittances require a currency exchange declaration and must be sourced to the subscribing member's own foreign bank account.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Corporate seal or provisional corporate seal
Identification documents of the representative and each subscriber
Bank capital deposit application form
Source-of-funds declaration and currency exchange declaration if foreign capital is introduced
Certificate of contribution received from the bank after deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced customer due diligence, the representative must submit a written explanation of the ASO and SEO agency business, a copy of the notarized articles, and proof of identity of the ultimate beneficial owner. Such queries can be cured by providing the requested documents in English or Korean translation within one banking day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing for Establishment Registration with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Office of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office in Seoul, Republic of Korea.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the territorial district of the registered office, the representative or an authorized attorney-in-fact must file the Application for Establishment Registration of a Limited Liability Company with the Registration Office of the District Court. The registrar will examine the notarized articles, the paid-in capital certificate, the seal impression card, the specimen signature, and all supporting resolutions. If the registration is granted, the registry will open the corporate registration record and issue a certified corporate register certificate. If the registrar issues a corrective order, the filer must cure the listed omissions within the statutory correction period, usually fifteen days, and pay no additional filing fee unless the examiner requires a new application. All signatures on the registration form must match the specimen signature kept at the registry.
required_dossiers: Application for Establishment Registration of a Limited Liability Company
Original notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of deposit of capital issued by the bank
Corporate seal impression card and specimen signature form
List of members and contribution amounts
Power of attorney if the filing is made by a representative or legal agent
Copy of the representative's identification document
Receipt of payment of court registration fee and registration tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a corrective order, the filer must submit the missing or corrected document within the prescribed correction period, generally fifteen days. If the application is rejected, the filer may prepare a corrected application and pay a reduced revision fee, or file an immediate appeal against the rejection order where allowed by the Commercial Registration Rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, Employment, and Operational Compliance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service District Office, local employment insurance authorities, and the licensed bank maintaining the corporate operating accounts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the court registration certificate is issued, the managing director must complete post-incorporation registration duties. Within twenty days of establishment, the company must file a business registration opening report with the competent National Tax Service District Office for corporate tax, VAT, and VAT invoices. The company must also obtain a corporate seal card, register any trademarks or service marks, open operational foreign currency accounts, and complete employer registrations for national pension, health insurance, unemployment insurance, and industrial accident insurance. The company must then notify its bank of the corporate registration certificate and activate digital banking. The managing director must also file the paid-in capital report with the court if required by the Commercial Act and maintain the corporate minute book and member register for inspection.
required_dossiers: Certified corporate register certificate issued by the court
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Business registration application form
Lease contract or documentary proof of registered office address
Corporate seal card and specimen signature
Identification certificate of the managing director
Bank account confirmation and payment infrastructure onboarding documents, including Wise B2B or Payoneer forms if used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office questions the lease address or the substance of the digital agency business, the managing director should submit a lease registration certificate, an explanation of the ASO and SEO localization services, and a corrected business registration application. If filing deadlines are missed, the company should use the National Tax Service voluntary correction procedure to minimize late filing and non-filing penalties.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea - HomeTax System (https://www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) in South Korea, the statutory procedure to obtain a Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT registration number is as follows: (1) Prepare the required documents, including the certificate of incorporation, articles of association, passport copies of the representative director, and a power of attorney if applicable; (2) Submit the application for business registration (사업자등록신청서) to the local district tax office (세무서) having jurisdiction over the entity's registered address, either in person or via the HomeTax online portal; (3) Upon approval, the NTS issues a Business Registration Certificate (사업자등록증) containing the 10-digit TIN, which also serves as the VAT registration number; (4) The entity must also register for the electronic tax invoice system (e-Tax Invoice) and, if applicable, for the cash receipt system; (5) The entire process typically takes 3-5 business days, and no minimum capital is required.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) acting under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with regulatory oversight from the Ministry of Strategy and Finance and operational supervision through designated foreign exchange banks and the Korea Financial Telecommunications and Clearing Institute (KFTC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a legally floating but administratively anchored convertibility regime. The current account is highly convertible for services, including app store optimization, digital marketing, localization fees, and other intangible trade activities. Such payments are freely made through designated foreign exchange banks provided the underlying transaction is genuine and the proper purpose code is declared in the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). The capital account is also substantially liberalized for inward direct investment; a non-resident shareholder may inject capital into a Korean Yuhan Hoesa without prior BOK approval, but must complete the requisite investment declaration and report through a domestic bank to obtain a certificate of foreign exchange banking. Profit remittance is permitted through dividend distributions, yet the outflow must be supported by audited financial statements, tax payment certificates, board resolutions, and a corresponding FEIS report; the remitting bank will screen for underlying economic substance and anti-money laundering risks. While there are no blanket surrender requirements for export receipts, all export and service proceeds must be repatriated within the statutory settlement window and are subject to transaction-level monitoring. The Korean won is not a fully freely convertible offshore currency; non-residents cannot freely trade it through unlicensed offshore venues, and onshore FX derivatives are limited to hedging purposes rather than speculative positions. Overall, capital suffices for routine treasury management, but compliance officers must maintain rigorous supporting dossiers for every cross-border wire to avoid automatic rejection or regulatory referral.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Direct fintech EMI service such as Wise Business, Payoneer, or similar neobank rails are not legally permitted to act as standalone bank account providers for a resident Korean corporate entity. Korea requires any entity providing foreign exchange business to be authorized as a foreign exchange bank or hold a limited payment service license with strict regulatory scope; EMIs are generally barred from opening domestic won-denominated operational accounts or foreign currency settlement accounts for a Yuhan Hoesa without partnering with a licensed Korean bank. The practical viability is Low to Medium: Wise and Payoneer may be used only as auxiliary payout channels for outbound contractor or software vendor payments, but the primary corporate treasury and capital verification must happen through a Tier-1 Korean commercial bank. Any attempt to route statutory equity contributions through an offshore EMI will fail the capital verification and bank onboarding process because the source of funds cannot be transparently matched to an FEIS investment declaration. Therefore, the treasury blueprint should treat all fintech EMIs as subordinated disbursement utilities, never as a substitute for the Korean banking relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa, physical presence is effectively mandatory for the statutory director and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) during the initial corporate account opening. Korean banks typically require at least one director who is named on the company registration document to appear in-person at a domestic branch, bringing original board resolution, seal certificates, certified passport and foreign registration card or proof of legal stay in Korea. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not permitted for a Korean LLC with no existing bank relationship. A remote video interview can supplement, but cannot replace, the initial face-to-face verification. The bank will also require the company to evidence a functional office address in Korea, which often means a physical lease, utility bill, and employer confidentiality registration. For an app growth agency with intangible services, the branch manager and compliance officer must be satisfied that the entity has real substance such as domestic staff, a local tax registration, and operational records, rather than acting as a shell with minimal presence. Under the anti-money laundering provisions of the Financial Transaction Reports Act, any failure or evasion of the in-person KYC interview is a critical blocker.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between the non-resident shareholder identity, the registered officer list, and the ultimate beneficial ownership disclosed in the Korean corporate registry, especially where the shareholder is a Hong Kong or Singapore holding vehicle with passive ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A certified corporate register from the shareholder's home jurisdiction; up-to-date register of beneficial ownership with screenshots of names and ownership chains; a board resolution designating the ultimate beneficial owner as a signatory; audited financial statements for the holding entity; a profile letter from the shareholder's upstream commercial bank confirming the source of subscription funds; and sworn declaration that no nominee shareholding exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The injected paid-in capital amount appears inconsistent with the stated business size of an ASO and SEO localization agency, creating suspicion of round-tripping, layering, or currency smuggling, particularly when the company will later make overseas vendor payments for ad inventory and app store accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A detailed business plan showing the app growth pipeline, expected monthly cumulative traffic volumes, planned SaaS subscription tools, localization subcontractor fee schedule, and ad wallet funding matrix; prior year client contracts and invoices from the shareholder network that demonstrate business rationale; source-of-wealth records for the contributed funds such as dividend vouchers, payroll records, and asset sale agreements; and a funding flow chart prepared by the receiving bank showing each wire message traceable to the original investor account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The target business is a low-touch digital marketing agency with a high proportion of payments to foreign subcontractors and platforms, which resembles a money service business or unlicensed money remitter, especially if the entity will receive large sums from app publishers and then disburse to overseas search engine vendors without clear contractual value.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete service agreement repository with each client naming the precise deliverables, performance metrics, app store keywords, localization languages, and timelines; signed master service agreements with each ad platform and translation vendor; system-generated ad campaign reports and proof of access rights to client app store consoles; a monthly cash-flow forecast matching incoming client payments to outgoing vendor payments; a written declaration that the entity does not engage in money remittance, foreign exchange dealings, or virtual asset services beyond its stated marketing scope; and a KYC questionnaire detailing the commercial model in Korean law terms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Korean bank compliance teams may flag a foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa lacking physical substance if no local employees, no rent, no payroll, and no local operating history are shown at onboarding, which is a classic shell company indicator.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Draft employment contracts for the Korean general manager and local marketing lead; certificate of business establishment and Korea Employment Insurance reporting; a certified copy of the lease agreement for a dedicated office environment with bathroom and non-shared facilities; municipal wastewater and electricity bills under the company name; the initial FEIS investment declaration and capital verification certificate; and a written explanation of the operational calendar showing how app store optimization, ASO keyword tagging, localization quality control, and client reporting will be performed inside Korea.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity injections must be received by a designated foreign currency account at a licensed Korean bank using SWIFT MT103 with the investor's full legal name, purpose of remittance clearly stated as capital contribution, and the FEIS transaction identification number generated after the investment declaration. The wire narrative should reference the Yuhan Hoesa name, the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act reporting reference, and the specific Korean corporate registration number to avoid quarantine. For a Korean LLC with no minimum statutory capital, the shareholder can contribute a practical working capital amount typically between KRW 100 million and KRW 300 million; an amount higher than the operational demonstrator will trigger additional source-of-funds review. After receipt, funds must remain in escrow until the bank issues a capital verification certificate (납입증명서), which is then submitted to the Korean court registry upon company registration; the same certificate is needed for the corporate bank account opening and later tax filings. The receiving bank will route the transaction through the BOK Foreign Exchange Information System, and the status must remain matched with the investment approval form. No inbound funds should be split into multiple small wires to avoid automatic reporting thresholds, and no Third-Party funding is acceptable; only the registered shareholder may inject equity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements and service expense payments from the Yuhan Hoesa, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for direct bank-to-bank treasury transfers to international vendors, ad platforms, and overseas localization partners. For larger, recurring app growth disbursements, a Commercial Letter of Credit is less appropriate because SE services are intangible; instead, the bank will likely require ordinary service LCs or bank payment obligations only under a special arrangement. Documentary collections are suitable when purchasing app store code assets or digital content licenses with transactional terms. The local Korean disbursement leg is cleared in Korean won via the KFTC wire system, which settles in near real-time. For foreign currency disbursements, the company must submit each payment instruction with the correct FEIS purpose code, an underlying contract, vendor invoice, and proof of service delivery. To avoid compliance friction, all outbound payments must be supported by a client-approved deliverable report, and the bank should establish a pre-approved recurring vendor list for high-frequency payments to Google, Apple, Meta, App Store index providers, and international SEO tool vendors. Any deviation from the expected payment profile of a digital marketing agency will be treated as suspicious transaction reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts between the Yuhan Hoesa and a licensed Korean bank, permitted only to cover genuine outstanding exposure on invoices, receivables, or capital flows with a maximum tenor aligned to the exposure document

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) transactions allowed only for non-resident counterparties through offshore channels or for Korean entities via bank-approved structured products when the underlying is a foreign currency account service trade asset, subject to the absence of speculative intent
Cross-currency swaps only for hedging long-term uncollateralized liability or investment exposure with a minimum notional above US$ 1 million and requiring a documented board risk assessment
Currency options for hedging known premium collection in USD and future Korean won operating expenses, approved only with rupee test and board-approved FX risk policy
Natural hedging through segmented foreign currency liquidity pools at the bank, where matched accounts in USD, EUR, RMB, and JPY are used to settle vendor liabilities before any won conversion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax interim prepayment return (mid-term corporate tax payment and return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (Korean Internal Revenue Service)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar fiscal year, on or before 31 August of the current fiscal year; for a non-calendar fiscal year, within two months after the first six months of the fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty of 20% of the deficient intermediate corporate tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-3; late-payment surcharge of 0.03% per day from the due date; compulsory tax collection and asset seizure upon sustained delinquency; Korea has no administrative strike-off but continued non-compliance can lead to business registration cancellation and asset auction.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax final return and local corporate income tax surcharge
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service for the national corporate income tax return; local corporate income tax surcharge is filed simultaneously through the National Tax Service and remitted to the competent local government treasury.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of the year following a calendar fiscal year; for a non-calendar fiscal year, within three months after the fiscal-year end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file: additional tax equal to 20% of the deficient tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-3; underreporting: additional tax of 10% of the understated tax, increased to 40% if concealment is done by an unlawful method; late-payment surcharge of 0.03% per day; asset seizure, compulsory collection, public listing as a delinquent corporation, and possible business registration cancellation by the National Tax Service.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax preliminary return for the first and third calendar quarters
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For the January-March quarterly period, on or before 25 April; for the July-September quarterly period, on or before 25 October; zero-rated export services must be supported by export evidence and included in the same electronic VAT return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a VAT preliminary return triggers an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid VAT; late-payment surcharge of 0.03% per day; incomplete export documentation can jeopardize zero-rating and cause assessment with additional 10% understatement penalty; continued non-filing can lead to compulsory collection and suspension of tax clearance certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax final return for the second and fourth calendar quarters
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For the April-June quarterly period, on or before 25 July; for the October-December quarterly period, on or before 25 January of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a VAT final return triggers an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid VAT; late-payment surcharge of 0.03% per day; underreported zero-rated exports attract 10% underreporting additional tax if not corrected and 40% in fraudulent cases; repeated non-compliance can result in asset seizure and criminal referral.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Monthly payroll income tax withholding remittance and social insurance contribution payments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service for wage withholding tax; National Pension Service for national pension; National Health Insurance Service for health insurance; Korea Employment Information Service for employment insurance; Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service for industrial accident insurance.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly payroll withholding tax and social insurance premiums are generally due by the 10th day of the following month; annual payroll income tax year-end settlement must be completed and delivered to employees by the last day of February following the calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to withhold and remit payroll income tax exposes the employer to a withholding additional tax of 3% of the unremitted amount plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.03%; social insurance authorities can impose late-payment charges and administrative fines; prolonged delinquency can trigger compelled collection from employer bank accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-invested company annual status report and change report (applicable only if the Yuhan Hoesa is a foreign-invested company under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual foreign-investment status report within 30 days after the end of the fiscal year, i.e., by 30 January for a calendar fiscal year; any change in foreign shareholding or transfer of a foreign investor's interest must be reported within 30 days of the transaction.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines for non-reporting or false reporting; revocation or clawback of foreign-investment tax incentives and customs-duty benefits; potential invalidation or cancellation of the foreign-investment registration; remediation demanded by MOTIE/KOTRA before enforcement action.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent certified public accountant audit under the Korean Act on External Audit and Accounting of Companies applies where the Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) has total assets equal to or exceeding KRW 12,000,000,000, approximately USD 9,000,000, as of the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year; is a stock-listing-market company or publicly offered corporation; or is otherwise designated by the Financial Services Commission or Securities and Futures Commission under the External Audit Act and its Enforcement Decree. Turnover and employee headcount are not standalone audit triggers under the current Korean statutory audit framework. Entities below the statutory audit threshold must still prepare financial statements in accordance with Korean accounting principles and attach them to the corporate income tax return; Korean transfer-pricing documentation rules may further require related-party transactional records and, in specified cases, a separate CPA review or tax-authority audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: External audit targets must apply K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) or, where permitted for private companies, Korean GAAP as prescribed by the Korean Accounting Standards Board; all statutory audits are performed in accordance with Korean Standards on Auditing; corporate tax bases are computed in accordance with the Corporate Tax Act and the Framework

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax headline rate on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion, plus 10% local income tax surcharge, producing 26.4% top aggregate headline; progressive rates of 9%, 19%, and 21% apply to lower tranches
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: General R&D tax credits under the Special Tax Reduction Control Act Article 10 for qualifying localization and software development; SME reduced rates and cash incentives may apply if Yuhan Hoesa qualifies as a small or medium enterprise; no patent box regime applies and the Seoul ASO/SEO agency is not eligible for free-zone income tax holidays absent special foreign investment designation; loss carryforward available for 5 years as specified

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Calculation Statement (Corporate Tax Return) filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax system, with attached international transaction integrated report and financial statements
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly prepayment declarations are made during the fiscal year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the end of each fiscal year under Article 60(1) of the Corporate Tax Act; a December 31 fiscal year-end return is due by March 31 of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity identification: business registration number, corporate name Yuhan Hoesa, head office address, representative director, fiscal year, and tax classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean LLC as a domestic corporation with unrestricted foreign ownership. Disclose each non-resident shareholder in the shareholder register and include country of residence codes and foreign ownership percentages, as these fields support later dividend withholding tax and treaty relief checks.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales and total income: all revenue from ASO, SEO localization, app growth campaign management, multilingual content services, and client reimbursement billings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all global fee income in Korean won under K-IFRS; do not net Wise or Payoneer transaction fees; include intercompany service fees from any foreign related party at arm's length. Cross-border receipts routed through payment rails must be fully accrued, and any understatement is treated as a taxable return omission.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable income and adjustment lines: tax-exempt dividends, non-business receipts, capital gains deferrals, and items excluded from the tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean LLC should not classify client localization subsidies as non-taxable unless a specific statutory exemption applies. For non-resident shareholders, this box is not used to exclude repatriated profits; profit distribution is characterized as dividend income at the shareholder level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: salaries, subcontractor costs, advertising media purchases, software licenses, office rent, depreciation, professional fees, and ordinary business operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim deductions only with valid tax invoices and evidence of actual service receipt. Payments to foreign related parties for marketing, IP licensing, or management services must satisfy the arm's length standard; absent a transfer pricing analysis, deductions can be disallowed and treated as cross-border constructive dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base calculation: gross income minus non-taxable income minus deductible expenses, then reduced by the allowed loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: After adjustments, the taxable base is computed under the Entity Level Taxation model for the Korean LLC. Since Yuhan Hoesa is a resident company, its worldwide income is taxable in Korea; foreign-source service income is included unless an exemption or foreign tax credit applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculated corporate tax at statutory progressive rates applied to taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the Korean domestic rate schedule: 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% over that, 21% for higher brackets, and 24% on the largest bracket. The same national tax calculation applies regardless of non-resident shareholding; there is no branch-level tax because this is a resident Korean entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, reductions, foreign tax credits, and minimum tax additions: R&D credits, employment credits, foreign taxes paid abroad, and advance withholding credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach supporting schedules for any R&D credit. Where foreign client countries withheld income tax on Korean service fees, claim foreign tax credits through the associated schedule; credits cannot exceed the Korean corporate tax attributable to that foreign-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total national corporate income tax payable before local surtax and prepayment offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate the resulting national tax after credits and then add the 10% local income tax surcharge in Box 9. For non-resident shareholders, no tax is collected at this stage on their shares; their tax arises only on actual dividend distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local income tax surcharge, prepayment installment offsets, and final balance due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter quarterly prepayments already deposited with the National Tax Service. If the final annual return shows a balance due, it must be paid by the filing deadline; any unpaid amount accrues daily late-payment surcharges. Non-resident shareholder withholding remains separate from the entity's final income tax settlement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attachments and declarations: statutory financial statements, audit reports if applicable, international transaction integrated report, transfer pricing forms, and related-party transaction disclosures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the International Transaction Integrated Report if cross-border related-party transactions exceed the statutory threshold. Declare all non-resident shareholders, their dividend withholding entitlements, and whether Tax Residency Certificates and beneficial ownership forms have been obtained. Deficiencies here trigger transfer pricing penalties and treaty relief denial.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or failure to file the Corporate Tax Return triggers an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid tax for non-filing, 10% for underreporting, and 40% for fraudulent underreporting, plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.025% on unpaid tax; failure to attach transfer pricing documentation attracts separate penalties of up to 10% of the understated related-party income; deliberate tax evasion through false invoices or offshore concealment exposes the company to criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with fines up to twice the evaded tax and imprisonment of responsible directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate withholding on outbound dividends: 20% national corporate income tax withholding under Article 98(1) of the Corporate Tax Act plus 2% local income tax surcharge
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before any dividend remittance, the non-resident shareholder must file an Application for Exemption from or Reduction of Withholding Tax under Tax Treaty with the National Tax Service through HomeTax, providing a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the shareholder's competent tax authority, a signed beneficial ownership declaration, evidence that the shareholder has real substance and is not a conduit, and a certified copy of the corporate register of the foreign shareholder; the Korean payor must verify the treaty entitlement and either apply the reduced rate before remittance or, if full withholding was applied, the shareholder may file a refund claim with the National Tax Service within three years of the withholding date
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory outbound withholding on royalties and interest is 20% national tax plus 2% local surcharge, aggregating 22%; bilateral Korean Double Tax Agreements typically reduce interest and royalty withholding to 10%-15%, and certain Korean treaties exempt qualifying government or financial institutions from interest withholding; treaty relief requires the same Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership procedure as dividends.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10,000,000,000 for the mandatory Local File relating to cross-border transactions with foreign related parties; KRW 100,000,000,000 consolidated revenue for the Master File; KRW 1,000,000,000 aggregate international related-party transactions triggers the annual International Transaction Integrated Report attached to the Corporate Tax Return
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply Caribbean-style ESR, but substance is mandatory under the general anti-abuse substance-over-form doctrine of Article 14 of the Framework Act on National Taxes and the controlled foreign company regime of the International Tax Adjustment Act; Core Income-Generating Activities for this ASO/SEO localization agency must be performed in Korea, including campaign strategy, keyword localization, content translation management, client negotiation, media buying decision-making, and contract execution, with actual local staff, office premises, bank accounts, and business records; a paper Korean entity lacking these functions will be disregarded or recharacterized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating ASO/SEO service revenue by routing global client fees through Wise, Payoneer, or a foreign holding account and recording only net expense reimbursement in the Korean LLC's books, while paying fictitious subcontractors for services never actually rendered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 76(1) of the Corporate Tax Act, fraudulent failure to report or underreporting carries a 40% additional tax on the unpaid national tax, plus the 10% local surcharge and 0.025% daily late-payment interest; under Article 3(1) of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, willful evasion is punishable by imprisonment up to three years or a fine not exceeding twice the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where the representative director caused the concealment or false invoicing; the director becomes jointly and secondarily liable for the entire corporate tax deficiency through the National Tax Collection Act, personal bank accounts and residences can be seized, the director may be placed on a departure-restriction blacklist with a travel ban, and criminal conviction carries imprisonment up to three years with personal fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating Yuhan Hoesa as a conduit shell with no employees, no Korean office, no substantive decision-making, and no local financial records, while the foreign parent or a non-resident beneficial owner artificially invoices royalties or service fees into the Korean entity and immediately strips out all profits through treaty-protected dividends or management fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service will recharacterize the arrangement under the substance-over-form doctrine and the integrated international transaction rules, disallow the artificial deductions, reclassify the amounts as constructive dividends, impose a 40% fraudulent underreporting additional tax, and deny the benefit of Korean tax treaties under domestic anti-abuse provisions; treaty relief can be refused even where a Tax Residency Certificate exists.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who signs false accounts for a shell company is exposed to civil asset restitution and personal secondary tax liability; the tax authority can freeze personal assets and impose a departure-restriction travel ban; in aggravated cases, the director is subject to criminal prosecution for tax evasion using a sham entity, with imprisonment risk and joint responsibility for penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold Tax on Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Yuhan Hoesa declares and pays dividends, royalties, or interest to non-resident shareholders or foreign related parties without deducting the mandatory withholding tax, or withholds at a treaty rate without collecting a valid Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership documentation, causing unreported outbound remittance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withholding agent is personally responsible for the uncollected tax under Article 97 of the Corporate Tax Act; Article 76(6) of the Corporate Tax Act imposes an additional tax of 10% of the undeposited withholding amount, plus daily late-payment interest of 0.025% from the due date; the foreign recipient also remains liable for the under-withheld tax through the collection process.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize dividend remittance without lawful withholding are treated as responsible withholding agents and can be assessed personally for the unpaid withholding tax and penalties; repeated willful non-withholding is treated as embezzlement of state tax revenue and can lead to criminal fines, imprisonment, personal asset attachment, and a travel-ban blacklist preventing the director from leaving Korea.
